Lost Features 6 11-5 D Collins Jack G Gilligan (5) 100-1 - 18 - Nothing in her four outings suggests she has any chance in a maiden. Blues Street 4 11-4h1 G Cromwell Kieren Buckley 20-1 - - - E66,000 store purchase as a 3yo; second foal; Blue Bresil gelding out of a Flat/hurdles winner by Jeremy; hooded for debut; trainer saddles two others who have shown ability. Granlahan 4 11-4 A McGuinness Patrick M O'Brien (5) 66-1 - 32 74 Beaten a long way in maidens at Punchestown and Cork; three-figure odds on both occasions. Betty's Glen 4 10-11 J Hanlon - - - Remote fifth of six at Punchestown on only bumper start; can be ruled out; first reserve. Page 1 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26 Me Wee Nanny Fran 4 11-4 G Cromwell - - 66 Down the field in two starts at Clonmel; 100-1 chance on latest; in good hands but not a likely winner at this stage; second reserve. Mirfaq 4 11-4 G Cromwell - - 56 25-1 chance when down the field at Cork on debut, will need to pick up more experience; third reserve.

Jack Kennedy's mount GREY JUDE will not need to improve much on the form of two Cork runs in November to take this maiden. The two most likely to test him are The Store Boy, a faller in a chase last time, and Endless Talking, a point winner likely to be suited by drying ground. [Alan Sweetman] Page 2 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26

Survivors Sister 7 11-7 P J Gilligan Jack G Gilligan (5) 16-1 105 105 121 Was keeping on when falling at the last in a 2m3f handicap at Limerick in December, went up 11lb for winning a weak 2m5f contest at the same venue in February; struggled at Fairyhouse later that month; not the most reliable sort. Piccolo Player 5 11-6 J Ryan Michael Kenneally (5) 12-1 104 100 115 Heavy-ground maiden winner last November; has failed to run to market expectations at Gowran and Limerick on his last two starts; needs to find extra Chanceawetmorning 6 11-4 G Elliott Jack Kennedy 13-1 102 84 110 11-race maiden; second of 12 finishers when a beaten favourite at Fairyhouse (2m4f, soft) in January; flopped when favourite at Ayr last month; first appearance for Gordon Elliott now Desert Haven 6 11-4t N Meade Donagh Meyler 7-2 102 94 118 Two respectable Flat runs last month; 0-11 over hurdles; comes into the reckoning following an improved display that saw him finish fifth of 21 in a stronger race than this at Fairyhouse. Jury Belle 5 11-4 J Hanlon Philip Byrnes 14-1 102 55 111 Second in a bumper in Britain last summer; had hinted at handicap potential in maidens before a moderate run at Clonmel a month ago. McLoughlin 4 11-1tp1 G Cromwell Conor Stone-Walsh 10-1 107 50 98 80-rated Flat maiden, placed twice in soft-ground maidens last back-end; yet to show an equivalent standard over hurdles; tongiue-tie on now as well as cheekpieces worn for his best Flat runs; could become competitive on handicap debut. Must Meet Cecil 8 11-3v C M Collins Carl Millar (5) 101 110 118 Five-time winner over hurdles; now on a long losing sequence since a claiming race success at Tramore just over a year ago; out of his depth in a Flat maiden last time; this is more realistic; first reserve. Page 3 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26 Coolboy Christy 5 11-2 P Rothwell 100 104 114 Promising fourth in a novice handicap hurdle at Leopardstown before a lesser effort at Downpatrick, when almost 7l behind third-placed Metamrpheus; second reserve. Metamorpheus 7 11-2 A McNamara 100 111 116 No success since a Punchestown maiden hurdle win (2m, heavy) three years ago; ran well from time to time when trained by Richard O'Brien; signs of a return to form when third at Downpatrick; in front of Coolboy Christy then; third reserve.

Dual Flat winner DESERT HAVEN has a realistic chance based on his fifth placing in a 21-runner contest at Fairyhouse last time. He has a clear edge over Kabylia on that running, but Gavin Cromwell's mare is respected as a course bumper winner with useful form in maiden hurdles. Chanceawetmorning could not be ruled out on his first run for Gordon Elliott. Another to consider is Malbay Madness, who won this race last year and scored again here in May. [Alan Sweetman] Page 4 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26

Euro Maker 5 11-1 A Murray NON-RUNNER 87 86 101 Non-runner. winner on better ground in the autumn, POURQUOI POI (nap) hasn't been seen since running a creditable race off his current mark in November. He has the aid of Jack Kennedy in the saddle and looks a big player in a race where few appeal. The Dancen Kid and The Toothpicker may give the selection most to do. [Denis Harney] Page 6 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26

point-to-point winner in November, GINO BELLA has been knocking on the door under rules since and may get it done here with Peter Smithers reducing her burden. Jack Kennedy rides Jaadil, who showed good progression last autumn, including a win but doesn't have the benefit of a run. A record of 0-20 over hurdles is off-putting but Hidalgo Des Mottes has run well in defeat and has a top claimer aboard. [Denis Harney] Page 8 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26

La Tene 8 10-1 J Ryan Michael Kenneally (5) 16-1 73 60 102 Took a step forward in a 2m3f handicap hurdle at Clonmel (soft) on latest, outpaced and rallying for a 7l third; way below that level over fences at Tramore last time (2m, yielding). Appian Way 10 10-0 M Flynn 72 84 100 Second reserve; no wins since 2022 and outings this year have been poor. Clever Court 5 10-5p1 P Rothwell 77 56 104 Third reserve; No sign of winning potential yet; outsider when pulled up at Fairyhouse in January; cheekpieces go on now.

Plenty with claims but a chance is taken on MICKEY HULIE. The dual-point-to-point winner was beaten just a neck at Naas last month and his moderate third eight days later may have come too soon. Live To Laugh will be popular given he runs off an 18lb lower hurdles mark following dual chase wins recently. Coppola and Sean Mc are others of interest. [Denis Harney] Page 10 spotlightkilbeggan 24.04.26

good second at this venue 12 months ago and another respectable run at Cork last month are enough to give the vote to GAOTH CHUIL who achieved a career-high mark of 136 over hurdles.
